title: Frontend project init: package.json, index.html, tsconfig.json, bun install
description:
## What
Initialize the Vite+React+TypeScript frontend project with the minimum boilerplate files needed before any component can be built or tested.

## Files to create
1. frontend/package.json — dependencies: react, react-dom, typescript, @vitejs/plugin-react, @types/react, @types/react-dom
2. frontend/index.html — standard Vite entry with <div id="root"> and <script type="module" src="/src/main.tsx">
3. frontend/tsconfig.json — standard Vite React TypeScript config

## Then run
cd frontend && bun install

## Key rules (AGENTS.md)
- Bun for package management. Never npm, yarn, or pnpm.
- vite.config.ts already exists with port 5274 and strictPort: true
- types.ts already exists with all TypeScript interfaces

## Why
Without these files, Vite cannot start and no component can render. Every frontend component bead implicitly depends on this setup existing. This is not "inventing work" — it's the minimum setup implied by the spec's choice of Vite+React+TypeScript.

## Considerations
- Keep dependencies minimal. The spec doesn't mention any CSS framework, but Tailwind classes appear in the spec (bg-yellow-200 for evidence highlighting). Add Tailwind if needed, or use inline styles.
- The spec uses className="bg-yellow-200" for evidence highlighting (line 1668), which implies Tailwind. Consider adding it.
close_reason: Created package.json, index.html, tsconfig.json. bun install succeeded (68 packages). Typecheck passes.

title: Sunday checklist: security grep — no PHI in codebase
description:
## What
Run the security grep and verify output is empty. Sunday checklist lines 1785-1789.

## Command (verbatim from spec)
grep -r "PHI\|patient_name\|ssn\|date_of_birth" \
    data/ backend/ frontend/src/ \
    --include="*.py" --include="*.tsx" \
    --include="*.json" --include="*.md"

## Expected result
Empty output. If anything matches, it must be removed before the interview.

## Why
This is a mock healthcare app. There must be zero PHI-adjacent fields anywhere in the codebase. Even synthetic data shouldn't use real-sounding PII field names. An interviewer scanning the code should see clean, compliant patterns.

## Definition of Done
AGENTS.md line 727-733: security grep returns empty.

title: Phase 2 gate: case-002 end-to-end with live model calls
description:
## What
Phase 2 gate: live pipeline produces correct results for case-002 reliably. Spec lines 1452-1454, 1759-1760.

## Gate criteria
- GET /runs/{run_id} resolves by actual run_id (not mock ID)
- case-002 output matches expected.json reliably:
  - action_type: "request_missing_documents"
  - missing_items includes "signed physician order within 30 days" and "progress notes within 30 days"
  - should_escalate: false
  - confidence >= 0.75
  - evidence_doc_ids include "denial-letter" and "notes"
- case-003 produces should_escalate: true with live model calls
- Pipeline completes in reasonable time (under 30 seconds for 3 calls)

## Why
Phase 2 replaces mock data with real Anthropic API calls. This is the transition from demo prototype to working system. The gate ensures the model actually produces correct, reliable outputs before we build the event persistence layer.

## What's involved
- anthropic_client.py: call_model() wrapper with error handling
- pipeline.py: 3-call orchestration (extract_facts → analyze_gap → draft_next_action)
- policy_search.py: keyword-based policy retrieval (no model, no vector DB)
- main.py: POST /runs updated to call live pipeline instead of loading mock_run.json
- Verification against expected.json for all 3 cases

## Considerations
- Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in environment
- Model: claude-sonnet-4-6 (AGENTS.md line 81)
- At most 3 model calls per run (spec line 45-46)
- If should_escalate is true, only 2 calls (no draft_next_action)

title: Implement anthropic_client.py — call_model() wrapper
description:
## What
Create backend/app/providers/anthropic_client.py with a single call_model() entry point. Spec lines 1135-1160.

## Implementation
- import anthropic SDK
- from app.errors import PipelineError (import from errors.py, NOT pipeline.py)
- Single function: call_model(system_prompt: str, user_content: str) -> str
- Model: claude-sonnet-4-6
- Catches APITimeoutError, APIConnectionError, RateLimitError and wraps them as PipelineError
- Returns the text content of the model response

## Key rules (AGENTS.md + spec)
- pipeline.py imports ONLY call_model from anthropic_client.py (spec line 1157)
- Never import the anthropic SDK directly in pipeline.py
- PipelineError wraps the raw response and cause exception for debugging
- ANTHROPIC_API_KEY must be in environment (standard anthropic SDK behavior)

## Why
This is the only place the Anthropic SDK is touched. Centralizing it here means error handling, model selection, and retry logic live in one place. The spec is explicit: "Never import the Anthropic SDK directly in pipeline.py" (line 1158).

## Files
- backend/app/providers/anthropic_client.py (create)
- backend/app/errors.py (already exists — import PipelineError from here)
close_reason: anthropic_client.py already implemented by another agent. Verified: correct model, timeout, error handling, PipelineError wrapping. Added __init__.py for providers package.

title: Implement pipeline.py — three-call orchestration
description:
## What
Create backend/app/pipeline.py with the three-call pipeline orchestrator. Spec lines 1023-1170.

## Functions to implement

### Constants
- VERBATIM_QUOTE_RULE: shared rule string (spec line 1026-1029)
- EXTRACT_FACTS_SYSTEM: system prompt for call 1 (spec lines 1031-1038)
- ANALYZE_GAP_SYSTEM: system prompt for call 2 (spec lines 1040-1050)
- DRAFT_NEXT_ACTION_SYSTEM: system prompt for call 3 (spec lines 1052-1063)
- FILENAME_TO_TYPE: dict mapping filenames to CaseDocument types (spec lines 1065-1079)
  "denial-letter" → "denial_letter", "auth-request" → "auth_request", "notes" → "clinical_notes"
  The "notes" → "clinical_notes" mapping is a SEMANTIC RENAME — not derivable by pattern.

### Functions
1. load_documents(case_id: str) -> list[CaseDocument]
   - Read .md files from DATA_DIR / "cases" / case_id
   - Use FILENAME_TO_TYPE to map filenames to types
   - Skip files not in FILENAME_TO_TYPE (like meta.json, expected.json)

2. extract_facts(documents: list[CaseDocument]) -> CaseFacts
   - Call call_model() with EXTRACT_FACTS_SYSTEM and document texts
   - Parse JSON response, validate with CaseFacts.model_validate()
   - Wrap json.JSONDecodeError in PipelineError

3. analyze_gap(facts: CaseFacts, policy_sections: list[str], documents: list[CaseDocument]) -> CaseFindings
   - Call call_model() with ANALYZE_GAP_SYSTEM
   - Parse and validate as CaseFindings

4. draft_next_action(findings: CaseFindings) -> Recommendation
   - Only called when should_escalate is false
   - Call call_model() with DRAFT_NEXT_ACTION_SYSTEM
   - Parse and validate as Recommendation

5. make_run_id(case_id: str) -> str
   - return f"run-{case_id}-{datetime.utcnow().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}"
   - Mock IDs (run-case-*-mock) must NEVER appear in JSONL event logs

6. run_pipeline(case_id: str, facility_id: str) -> RunStatus
   - Orchestrator: load_documents → extract_facts → retrieve_policy_sections → analyze_gap → conditionally draft_next_action
   - Spec lines 1287-1313

## Key rules
- import json at top (spec line 1089)
- import ONLY call_model from anthropic_client (line 1157)
- from app.errors import PipelineError
- Use json.loads() for parsing model responses; wrap failures in PipelineError
- Structured logging: logger.info/warning/error, never print()
- DATA_DIR via pathlib

## Files
- backend/app/pipeline.py (create)
close_reason: pipeline.py implemented: load_documents with FILENAME_TO_TYPE, extract_facts, analyze_gap, draft_next_action, run_pipeline orchestrator. JSON fence stripping. All Pydantic typed returns.

title: Implement policy_search.py — keyword-based policy retrieval
description:
## What
Create backend/app/policy_search.py with keyword-based policy retrieval. Spec lines 1214-1235.

## Function signature
def retrieve_policy_sections(
    facility_id: str,
    service_requested: str,
    denial_reason: str,
    required_documents: list[str],
) -> list[str]

## Implementation
1. Read DATA_DIR / "policies" / f"{facility_id}.md"
2. Split by "## " headings into sections
3. Keyword match on: service_requested, denial_reason, required_documents
4. A section matches if ANY keyword appears (case-insensitive) in it
5. Return top 3 matching sections as list of strings
6. If zero sections match, return the first 2 sections from the file
   - Do NOT return the full file on zero-match — it floods model context (spec line 1229)
   - Policy files lead with their most general rules, making first sections the safest fallback
7. Empty policy context causes hallucinated findings — always return something

## Key rules
- Do NOT build a vector database (spec line 1234)
- Do NOT call any model for retrieval (spec line 1235)
- DATA_DIR via pathlib
- Structured logging

## Why
Pipeline calls this between extract_facts and analyze_gap. The policy sections are passed as context to the gap analysis model call. Without real policy context, the model hallucinates missing items.

## Files
- backend/app/policy_search.py (create)
close_reason: policy_search.py implemented: keyword-based section retrieval, splits by ## headings, returns top 3 matches or first 2 on zero match. Verified with case-002 data.

title: Replace POST /runs mock with live pipeline call
description:
## What
Update POST /runs in main.py to call run_pipeline() instead of loading mock_run.json. Spec lines 1260-1313.

## Changes to main.py
- Import run_pipeline from app.pipeline
- Read meta.json to get facility_id:
  meta_path = DATA_DIR / "cases" / case_id / "meta.json"
  if not meta_path.exists():
      raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="meta.json not found")
  with open(meta_path) as f:
      facility_id = json.load(f)["facility_id"]
- Call run_status = run_pipeline(case_id, facility_id)
- Seed state: state.seed(run_status.run_id, run_status.model_dump())
- Return run_status

## Add PipelineError handler
main.py catches PipelineError in a single handler and returns 422 (spec line 1190).
Never let json.JSONDecodeError or ValueError surface as unhandled 500s.

@app.exception_handler(PipelineError)
async def pipeline_error_handler(request, exc):
    return JSONResponse(status_code=422, content={"detail": str(exc)})

## Key rules
- Lifespan hook still seeds mock data for quick testing — do not remove it
- Live runs generate unique run_ids via make_run_id() — never reuse mock IDs
- state.seed() stores the live result for subsequent GET /runs/{run_id}

## Why
This is the core Phase 2 transition: from static mocks to live model calls. After this change, clicking "Run Review" in the UI triggers actual Anthropic API calls.

## Files
- backend/app/main.py (modify)
close_reason: POST /runs updated: reads meta.json for facility_id, calls run_pipeline, catches PipelineError as 422. Phase bumped to 2. Live test requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

title: Verify live pipeline output against expected.json for all 3 cases
description:
## What
Run the live pipeline against all 3 cases and verify outputs match expected.json. Spec line 1759.

## Verification matrix

### case-001 (happy path)
- expected_action_type: "approve_or_proceed"
- expected_missing_items: [] (empty)
- expected_should_escalate: false
- expected_confidence_min: 0.85
- expected_evidence_doc_ids: ["auth-request", "notes"]

### case-002 (main demo)
- expected_action_type: "request_missing_documents"
- expected_missing_items: ["signed physician order within 30 days", "progress notes within 30 days"]
- expected_should_escalate: false
- expected_confidence_min: 0.75
- expected_evidence_doc_ids: ["denial-letter", "notes"]

### case-003 (escalation)
- expected_should_escalate: true
- expected_missing_items: ["functional assessment within 60 days"]
- expected_recommendation_present: false (recommendation is null)
- expected_evidence_doc_ids: ["denial-letter", "notes"]

## How to verify
1. curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/runs -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"case_id": "case-001"}'
2. Compare each field against expected.json
3. Repeat for case-002 and case-003
4. Run multiple times to check reliability (LLM outputs vary)

## Why
This is the Phase 2 gate criterion: "case-002 produces correct recommendation reliably" (line 1760). If the model outputs don't match expected values, prompts need tuning before proceeding to Phase 3.

## Considerations
- LLM outputs are non-deterministic. "Reliably" means the structural decisions (should_escalate, missing items list) are consistent, not that exact wording matches.
- Confidence values may vary between runs. The threshold is a minimum, not an exact match.
- evidence_doc_ids checks that the model cites the correct source documents, not exact quotes.
acceptance_criteria:
1. case-001: action_type=approve_or_proceed, missing_items=[], should_escalate=false, confidence>=0.85, evidence includes auth-request and notes
2. case-002: action_type=request_missing_documents, missing_items includes physician order and progress notes, should_escalate=false, confidence>=0.75, evidence includes denial-letter and notes
3. case-003: should_escalate=true, missing_items includes functional assessment, recommendation is null, evidence includes denial-letter and notes
4. curl /health returns {"status": "ok", "phase": "2"} (CURRENT_PHASE updated from 1 to 2)

The spec (line 1427) requires the health phase to advance as gates pass. bd-7x4.6 covers the '3' update; the '1' to '2' update should happen as part of Phase 2 completion and be verified here.

title: Phase 1 gate: full 7-minute demo arc against mocked data
description:
## What
Verify the complete Phase 1 mock demo arc works end-to-end. This is the gate that must pass before ANY Phase 2 work begins.

## Gate criteria (from spec lines 1449-1451)
- All 7 backend routes respond correctly (health, cases, runs CRUD, replay, demo-fallback)
- Frontend renders all three panels (documents, recommendation, run history)
- Approval changes run status from approval_requested to approved
- Replay shows timeline with is_replay_response: true
- Escalated case-003 shows escalation notice, no draft, no approve button
- case-002 mock demo arc is performable in under 7 minutes

## Why this matters
This is the foundational quality gate. Phase 2 replaces mock data with live model calls — if the UI doesn't work against mocked data, live data will only add more failure modes. The spec explicitly says "gate before moving on" (line 1752).

## What's already done
- Steps 1-9: case documents, schemas, types, vite config all created and committed
- Step 10/11: main.py with 7 mocked routes, state.py — created, verified with curl, committed
- Backend serves mock data correctly

## What remains for this gate
- Step 12: Start uvicorn, verify all routes via curl (partially done, needs full frontend verification)
- Build frontend (api.ts, App.tsx, CaseListPage, RunPage, all 5 components)
- Smoke test the full demo arc in a browser

## Considerations
- This gate blocks ALL of Phase 2. Do not start anthropic_client.py, pipeline.py, or policy_search.py until this passes.
- The frontend build is the bulk of the remaining work for this gate.
- AGENTS.md says: after every meaningful code change, uvicorn restart + curl /health + browser smoke test.

## Files involved
- frontend/src/api.ts, App.tsx, main.tsx
- frontend/src/pages/CaseListPage.tsx, RunPage.tsx
- frontend/src/components/DocumentPanel.tsx, FactCards.tsx, GapAnalysisTable.tsx, RecommendationEditor.tsx, RunHistoryPanel.tsx

title: Write frontend/src/api.ts — typed fetch helpers
description:
## What
Create api.ts as the single source of truth for all API calls to the backend. Spec lines 1588-1625.

## Verbatim from spec
const API_BASE = "http://localhost:8000";

Four exported functions:
- postRun(caseId: string): Promise<RunStatus> — POST /runs with { case_id: caseId }
- postApprove(runId: string, draftText?: string): Promise<RunStatus> — POST /runs/{runId}/approve
- getReplay(runId: string): Promise<RunStatus> — GET /runs/{runId}/replay
- getCases(): Promise<{ case_id: string }[]> — GET /cases

## Key rules
- All components import from api.ts. Never write fetch() inline in components (spec line 1625).
- Import RunStatus from types.ts.
- Error handling: if (!res.ok) throw new Error with route info and status code.
- API_BASE is hardcoded to http://localhost:8000 per spec. No env var pattern for backend port in spec.

## Why
This is the contract layer between frontend and backend. Every component depends on these typed helpers. Creating it first prevents inline fetch() calls from creeping into components.

## Files
- frontend/src/api.ts (create)
- frontend/src/types.ts (import from — already exists)

title: Write RunHistoryPanel.tsx — event timeline with replay button and REPLAY badge

   Do not render null or throw on empty array (spec lines 1707-1709)

## Props
events: RunEvent[], isReplayResponse: boolean, onReplay: () => void

## Why
Run history is the audit trail visualization (demo arc 5:00-6:00). The REPLAY badge is specifically called out in the Sunday checklist (line 1780) and Definition of Done. The timeline must be readable — each event type should be visually distinct.

## Considerations
- Case-001 (happy path): 7 events ending with approval_requested
- Case-002 (main demo): 7 events ending with approval_requested, becomes 8 after approve
- Case-003 (escalated): 5 events ending with analysis_completed (no draft_generated, no approval_requested)

title: Write frontend/src/App.tsx — View union navigation
description:
## What
Create App.tsx with state-based navigation using a View union type. Spec lines 219-268.

## Verbatim from spec
type View =
  | { page: "cases" }
  | { page: "run"; caseId: string; runId: string };

Two views:
- CaseListPage receives onSelectCase: (caseId: string, runId: string) => void
- RunPage receives caseId, runId, and onBack: () => void

## Key rules (AGENTS.md + spec)
- No React Router. No URL routing. No window.location. No hard reload.
- View union discriminated on page field.
- CaseListPage.onSelectCase is called AFTER POST /runs succeeds — pass run_id from the response.
- Back button on RunPage returns to case list without hard reload.

## Why
The spec explicitly forbids React Router (line 268). State-based navigation keeps the demo simple — two views, one useState. The View union is the simplest possible implementation that satisfies the two-screen requirement.

## Dependencies
- Requires CaseListPage.tsx and RunPage.tsx to exist (or at minimum, stub exports)

## Files
- frontend/src/App.tsx (create — spec provides verbatim implementation)

title: Write CaseListPage.tsx — case list with Run Review button
description:

title: Write RunPage.tsx — three-panel layout orchestrator
description:
## What
Create RunPage.tsx as the orchestrator for the three-panel layout. Spec lines 1586-1709.

## Layout
Three side-by-side panels:
- Left: DocumentPanel (documents + policy sections + facility label)
- Center: FactCards + GapAnalysisTable + RecommendationEditor
- Right: RunHistoryPanel (events timeline + replay button)

## Behavior
- On mount: fetch run data via GET /runs/{runId} from api.ts
- Pass run data down to child components
- Handle approve: call postApprove() from api.ts, update local state with response
- Handle replay: call getReplay() from api.ts, update local state with response

title: Phase 3 gate: replay reconstructs same result without calling model
description:
## What
Phase 3 gate: JSONL event log persists all pipeline events, and replay.py reconstructs the same RunStatus from those events without calling any model. Spec line 1769.

## Gate criteria
- event_store.py writes JSONL events during each pipeline stage
- replay.py reads JSONL and reconstructs RunStatus identically
- GET /runs/{run_id}/replay returns reconstructed state with is_replay_response: true
- GET /runs/{run_id} resolves by actual run_id from JSONL (not just in-memory state)
- Replay never calls model providers or writes files
- REPLAY badge appears in right panel header
- Approved event shows final_recommendation as first-class event in timeline

## Why
The JSONL event log IS the audit trail. Without it, there is no evidence of what happened, what the model said, or what the human approved. Replay is the proof that the system is auditable — you can reconstruct any past run without calling the model again.

## What's involved
- event_store.py: JSONL append functions
- pipeline stage wiring: append events at each stage
- replay.py: read-only JSONL reconstruction
- main.py updates: GET /runs and GET /replay use JSONL-backed data

## Definition of Done items covered by this gate
- Replay reconstructs same result without calling the model
- REPLAY badge appears in right panel on replay
- Approve button becomes "Approved ✓" badge after approval
- GET /runs after approve returns approved state (not stale mock)

title: Implement event_store.py — JSONL append-only event log
description:
## What
Create backend/app/event_store.py with JSONL append functions. Spec lines 1458-1521.

## Implementation
- Storage path: DATA_DIR / "runs" / f"{run_id}.jsonl"
- One JSON object per line. Append only. Never rewrite or delete lines.
- Directory creation at module level (NOT inside a function):
  from pathlib import Path
  REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
  DATA_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "data"
  (DATA_DIR / "runs").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  This runs on import. Never assume the directory exists on a fresh clone.

## Function
def append_event(run_id: str, event_type: str, payload: dict) -> None:
    # Append a single event line to the JSONL file
    # Include type, timestamp (ISO 8601 with Z suffix), and payload

## Valid event types (v1 only) — spec lines 1470-1484
- run_started: {"run_id": "...", "case_id": "...", "facility_id": "..."}
- documents_loaded: {"documents": [full CaseDocument objects]}
- facts_extracted: {"facts": {full CaseFacts object}}
- policy_retrieved: {"retrieved_policy_sections": ["...", "..."]}
- analysis_completed: {"findings": {full CaseFindings object}}
- draft_generated: {"recommendation": {full Recommendation object}} (non-escalation only)
- approval_requested: {} (non-escalation only)
- approved: {"final_recommendation": {full final recommendation}} (non-escalation only)

## Key rules
- "rejected" is NOT a v1 event type (spec line 1481)
- "replay_requested" is NOT an event type (spec line 1482)
- is_replay_response is response metadata only — NEVER written to JSONL (spec line 1483)
- Event payloads MUST carry FULL objects for replay (spec line 1486). Truncated text = truncated UI.
- Structured logging, never print()

## Why
The JSONL log is the source of truth for the entire audit system. Every decision, every model output, every human action is recorded here. replay.py reads from this log. Without complete payloads, replay produces incomplete or broken UI.

## Files
- backend/app/event_store.py (create)

title: Wire event appends into pipeline stages
description:
## What
Add event_store.append_event() calls at each pipeline stage. Spec lines 1486-1521.

## Wiring points in pipeline.py (run_pipeline function)
1. After run_id created: append run_started event
2. After load_documents: append documents_loaded event (FULL document text, not truncated)
3. After extract_facts: append facts_extracted event (full CaseFacts as dict)
4. After retrieve_policy_sections: append policy_retrieved event
5. After analyze_gap: append analysis_completed event (full CaseFindings as dict)
6. If not escalated, after draft_next_action: append draft_generated event
7. If not escalated: append approval_requested event (empty payload)

## Wiring point in main.py (approve route)
8. After approval: append approved event with final_recommendation payload

## Key rules
- Use model_dump() to convert Pydantic objects to dicts for event payloads
- Event payloads must carry FULL objects (spec line 1486)
- Documents text must be FULL text passed to the model (spec line 1493)
- policy_retrieved always follows facts_extracted in the log (spec line 1501)
- Timestamps: datetime.utcnow().isoformat() + "Z"

## Why
Without event wiring, the JSONL log is empty. replay.py has nothing to reconstruct from. This is the bridge between the live pipeline and the persistence layer.

## Files
- backend/app/pipeline.py (modify — add event appends)
- backend/app/main.py (modify — add approved event append in approve route)

title: Implement replay.py — read-only JSONL reconstruction
description:
## What
Create backend/app/replay.py with read-only JSONL reconstruction. Spec lines 1524-1582.

## Required verbatim comment (must appear and never be removed)
# Replay is read-only reconstruction from persisted events.
# It must never call model providers or produce new side effects.

## Implementation
def replay_run(run_id: str) -> RunStatus:
    Read DATA_DIR / "runs" / f"{run_id}.jsonl" line by line.
    Parse each line as JSON. Wrap json.loads() in try/except json.JSONDecodeError —
    skip malformed lines with a warning log (crash mid-append produces partial lines).
    
    Rebuild RunStatus by processing events in order:
    - run_started.payload → seed run_id, case_id, facility_id
    - documents_loaded.payload.documents → populate documents
    - facts_extracted.payload.facts → populate facts
    - policy_retrieved.payload.retrieved_policy_sections → populate retrieved_policy_sections
    - analysis_completed.payload.findings → populate findings; if should_escalate, set status
    - draft_generated.payload.recommendation → populate recommendation
    - approval_requested → no state change
    - approved.payload.final_recommendation → replace recommendation, set status "approved"

## resolve_status function (separate — SRP)
def resolve_status(state: dict) -> str:
    if state.get("findings", {}).get("should_escalate"):
        return "escalated"
    if state.get("status") == "approved":
        return "approved"
    return "approval_requested"

## Key rules
- Set is_replay_response = True (response metadata only, never persisted to JSONL)
- Never call pipeline.py functions
- Never call anthropic_client.py
- Never write any new events or files
- state dict uses plain Python types from json.loads(), not Pydantic objects
- Structured logging for skipped lines

## Files
- backend/app/replay.py (create)

title: Update GET /runs/{run_id} to resolve by actual run_id from JSONL
description:
## What
Update GET /runs/{run_id} in main.py to resolve runs from JSONL event logs, not just in-memory state. Spec lines 1315-1323.

## Current behavior (Phase 1)
state.get(run_id) — returns None if not in memory (404).

## Required behavior (Phase 3)
1. First check state.get(run_id) — fast path for in-memory runs
2. If None, check if DATA_DIR / "runs" / f"{run_id}.jsonl" exists
3. If exists, call replay_run(run_id) to reconstruct from JSONL
4. If neither, return 404

## Why
After uvicorn restart, in-memory state is wiped. Without JSONL fallback, all past runs return 404. The JSONL file IS the persistent record. This change makes runs survive server restarts.

## Key rules
- Do NOT re-read mock_run.json on GET (spec line 1319). Mock seeding is lifespan-only.
- The JSONL-reconstructed response should NOT have is_replay_response: true — it's a normal GET, not a replay request.
- Or rather: this is an implementation decision. The spec says replay route sets it. GET route may or may not. Check spec line 1401-1410 vs 1315-1321.

## Files
- backend/app/main.py (modify GET /runs/{run_id})

title: Update GET /runs/{run_id}/replay to use JSONL reconstruction
description:
## What
Update GET /runs/{run_id}/replay in main.py to use replay.py for JSONL reconstruction. Spec lines 1400-1421.

## Current behavior (Phase 1)
state.get(run_id) → set is_replay_response = True → return. Simple pass-through.

## Required behavior (Phase 3)
1. Check if DATA_DIR / "runs" / f"{run_id}.jsonl" exists
2. If exists: call replay_run(run_id) from replay.py → returns RunStatus with is_replay_response: true
3. If not exists: fall back to state.get(run_id) with is_replay_response flag (for mock runs without JSONL)
4. If neither: return 404

## Why
True replay means reconstructing state from the JSONL event log, proving that the log alone is sufficient to reproduce the entire run. This is the core auditability claim.

## Key rules
- Never calls pipeline.py or any model provider (spec line 1420)
- Does not overwrite or change the persisted run status (spec line 1421)
- is_replay_response: true on the response (set by replay.py)
- REPLAY badge in the UI depends on this field being true

## Files
- backend/app/main.py (modify GET /runs/{run_id}/replay)
